note: The Python modules js/layer_a.js, js/image_meta.js, js/av_meta.js, js/stylometry.js and js/gumbel.js were ported from. scripts/check-upstream.mjs compares the live content against these hashes. The parity suite proves the ported behaviour still matches for the cases it covers; this catches the rest: new options, new formats, anything the fixtures do not exercise. When one moves, re-port it and update `sha256` in the same commit.
followUp: If the parity suite is still green, the change is probably additive — a new format or option the fixtures do not reach. Add fixtures covering it, or the gap stays invisible the next time too.

sources.comment: Deliberately partial: upstream #156 hardened the error handling around the external c2patool subprocess (a failed run is inconclusive, not 'no C2PA'). There is no c2patool and no run_optional_tools in a browser, so js/image_meta.js has nothing to mirror there. Partial for the same reason since upstream 8e16b822, which passes creationflags=subprocess_creationflags to every subprocess.run so a child process opens no console window on Windows: a browser starts no child processes. Everything else in this file is ported.

This port used to diverge here: upstream's _strip_moov_udta rebuilt an MP4 from the boxes that parsed and dropped everything after them, so a truncated download lost its media while the action list still said the tail was kept. Reported as guillaumemeyer/watermarks-remover#240 and fixed upstream by #242, which keeps the tail the same way and adds an inspection_incomplete flag that clean_av folds into still_has_ai_metadata. js/av_meta.js carries the same flag as inspectionIncomplete through both drivers, and tests/test_av_meta_parity.py now asserts the two agree. Partial in the same way image_meta.py is: inspect_av and clean_av take filesystem paths and use safe_write_bytes, which has no counterpart in a browser. clean_av's post-clean re-inspection is also not mirrored: the page inspects before cleaning and reports through the UI instead.
